name: Agent Delegation
description: Let the main agent delegate tasks to specialist agents

function.name: ask_agent
function.description: Delegate a task to a specialist agent. Chain multiple calls when needed. For a two-step PIPELINE where one specialist produces something and a DIFFERENT specialist consumes it (e.g. generate an image then email it, read a receipt then add it to expenses), use `handoff_to`/`handoff_directive` to run both in ONE call: the first agent's output (text + any image/file it produced) is passed straight to the second agent, and you DON'T run another turn to relay or re-route in between. The pipeline runs in the background — this call returns a task id immediately, and the second agent's reply is posted back to this chat as the final word when the chain finishes.

agent_id.description: The ID of the specialist agent to delegate to (the FIRST stage if you also pass handoff_to).

handoff_to.description: Optional id/name of a SECOND specialist to hand the first agent's result to, in the same call. Use for a producer→consumer pipeline (image agent → email agent; receipt-reader → expenses agent). The first agent runs, its reply and any file/image it produced are forwarded automatically to this agent, which then acts on them. This replaces the slower pattern of delegating to A, getting the result back, then delegating to B yourself — you author the whole chain once and the result comes back from the second agent. Only the coordinator may set this. The pipeline runs detached in the background: you get a task id back immediately, the user watches (and can stop) it via the task chip, and the second agent's final reply is posted back automatically.

handoff_directive.description: Required when handoff_to is set: one line telling the SECOND agent what to DO with the first agent's output. E.g. 'Email the generated image to the user as an attachment', 'Add this receipt's line items to expenses'. Whatever file/image the first agent produced is attached to the context automatically, with its exact attachment id.

task.description: The exact task or question to give the specialist, INCLUDING the full content to act on — recipients, date ranges, amounts, the briefing/body text, the doc content. Be specific and complete. When asking an email agent to send a file from shared-docs, include the doc_id in the task and tell the agent to pass it as attachment_doc_ids to email_compose.

directive.description: One short line stating WHAT the specialist must DO — the action, not the content. E.g. 'Send an email to alex@example.com', 'Summarize these documents', 'Create a calendar event'. This is what selects the specialist's tools, so keep large content (the briefing text, the doc body, the list) in `task`, not here. STRONGLY recommended whenever `task` carries a big payload to act on (sending a long briefing, processing pasted content): it ensures the specialist gets its action tool (e.g. compose/send) instead of having it crowded out by the payload.

background.description: Set TRUE for long tasks where the user should be free to keep chatting while the specialist works: skill creation, code refactoring, research, configuration changes, deployments, and other multi-tool work. Coordinator-started background delegations are tracked by task id; when they finish, the coordinator is woken with that exact task id, original task, and result so it can continue any remaining workflow. Use FALSE only when you truly need the answer in this same model turn. Pipelines (handoff_to) run in the background by default; pass false only if you truly need the pipeline's result inside this same turn.

no_confirm.description: If true, instruct the specialist to skip its 'show draft and wait for approval' gate for this one delegation. Use when the user has explicitly authorized the action in the message that triggered this delegation (e.g. 'just send it', 'no need to confirm'). Defaults to false.

terminal.description: Only meaningful with handoff_to AND background:false (a foreground pipeline). When true (the default), the final agent's reply is delivered to the user AS your turn's answer without another model turn. Backgrounded pipelines (the default) always report their result back as a completed-task update instead.

function.name: list_execution_targets
function.description: Discover exact provider/model ids and supported reasoning-effort ids available to this account for spawned agents. Call this before spawn_worker whenever the user names a family, alias, provider, or effort level (for example Terra, Claude, Qwen, Grok, xhigh, or ultra) instead of guessing. Results are catalog-backed, account-filtered, and paged. An empty query lists all available targets; use provider/offset to page large catalogs.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive model/provider search, such as terra, qwen, grok, or claude opus.

provider.description: Optional exact configured provider id to search within.

refresh.description: When true, refresh configured provider catalogs before returning results. Use when the user asks for the latest catalog or a newly released model.

limit.description: Maximum targets to return in this page. Defaults to 20.

offset.description: Zero-based page offset. Use has_more to continue.

function.name: spawn_worker
function.description: Hire one background COORDINATOR WORKER only when the user explicitly asks for background or agent execution. Ordinary questions, news lookups, comparisons, long jobs, and normal tool actions stay in the current execution path unless the user opts into a worker. Give the worker one complete outcome, not one tiny lane. It may create child workstreams only when the user explicitly requested parallel agents; otherwise it remains a single worker. execution_targets may pin those user-counted agents to any configured provider/model combination; the hidden coordinator remains on the parent model and does not count. Explicit unavailable targets fail instead of inheriting. Repeated calls and browser Retry are durably coalesced. After launching every requested outcome, reply immediately; never call check_workers in that same turn. Use check_workers only for a later user status request and stop_worker to cancel.

task.description: The complete, self-contained job for the worker. It runs autonomously with no chance to ask you follow-ups, so include everything it needs and state exactly what 'done' looks like (e.g. 'Sort every email matching in:inbox has:nouserlabels into my existing labels, keep them in the inbox, repeat until INBOX DRAINED').

label.description: Short stable job label for the progress chip and duplicate protection (e.g. 'Sort whole inbox'). Use a distinct label for each intentionally parallel worker and reuse the same label if retrying.

worker_count.description: Exact number of child workstreams explicitly requested by the user for THIS outcome. The coordinator is additional and does not count. Preserve a user-specified count from 2–12 exactly. If the user asks for plural/parallel agents without a number (for example, 'Terra agents'), omit worker_count; never copy a suggested or adaptive 2–4 lane count into this property. Omitting it does not authorize automatic child fan-out.

execution_targets.description: Optional provider-neutral allocation for the agents the user requested. Each provider/model pair must be configured and available to this account. One entry with no count pins every requested child to that pair (or pins the sole detached worker when there is no fan-out). For an uncounted plural target such as 'Terra agents', use exactly one entry and omit both worker_count and this entry's count. For mixed targets, count defaults to 1 on each entry and the counts must sum exactly to worker_count or the exact model-qualified groups in the user's request. The hidden coordinator remains on the parent model and is not part of this allocation. Never invent, approximate, or silently replace a provider/model id.

provider.description: Exact configured provider id, such as openai-oauth, xai-oauth, anthropic, openrouter, ollama, lmstudio, or a configured compatible-provider id.

model.description: Exact model id from that provider's configured model catalog.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional exact reasoning-effort id explicitly requested for this target, such as low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or ultra. Use only a value returned for this exact provider/model by list_execution_targets; support differs by model and changes with provider catalogs. Omit this property when the user did not name an effort—do not send auto merely as a placeholder for the provider/model default. Send auto only when the user explicitly requests it and the target advertises it.

count.description: Number of user-counted agents on this exact provider/model pair. Omit for a single homogeneous entry (meaning all requested agents), including uncounted plural requests; never copy an adaptive 2–4 suggestion here. In a mixed allocation omission means 1.

function.name: parallel_work
function.description: Only when the user explicitly requested parallel agents for this outcome, centrally assign genuinely independent read-only workstreams, queue them under bounded concurrency, then receive every child result for synthesis. This is domain-neutral: lanes may cover sources, files, components, APIs, accounts, products, hypotheses, or other non-overlapping work. If the user explicitly requested parallelism without a count, choose 2–4 lanes adaptively. When the outcome carries an explicit count, work_items MUST contain exactly that many children (up to 12); the coordinator does not count. A carried homogeneous execution target applies to every child. Prefer omitting work_items[].execution for it; if repeated, omit reasoning_effort whenever the carried target has none and never use auto as a placeholder. A carried mixed allocation requires every item to name its exact execution provider/model, and the complete item multiset must match the allocation. With no carried allocation, omitting execution inherits the coordinator pair. Explicit targets are validated atomically and never fall back. work_items is the total child count, while max_parallelism only limits how many may run locally at once. Children gather/analyze evidence only; you remain the coordinator and final completion owner and must serialize any resulting writes yourself. Each item MUST reserve a stable generic claim so the runtime can prevent duplicate work. Children cannot recursively delegate.

goal.description: Short description of the shared outcome these independent lanes support.

max_parallelism.description: Optional local concurrency cap, never the requested worker total. Defaults to min(work_items, 4) for fairness across outcomes. It may be raised up to work_items when appropriate; the shared per-user scheduler still queues lanes above global capacity.

work_items.description: The complete child-worker plan. Its length is the total number of explicitly requested children: 2–4 when the user requested parallelism without a count, or exactly the explicit user-requested count when one was carried into this outcome.

task.description: Complete, standalone instructions and deliverable for this lane only.

execution.description: Exact provider/model for this child. Required on every item when a mixed allocation was carried from spawn_worker. For a homogeneous carried allocation, prefer omitting execution entirely; the server fills the required pair. If repeating a homogeneous pair, omit reasoning_effort when the carried target omits it—auto is not a placeholder. With no carried allocation, omission inherits the coordinator pair. An explicit unavailable pair fails the whole wave; it never inherits or falls back.

model.description: Exact model id from that provider's catalog.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional exact reasoning-effort id carried for this child. It must match the authorized allocation and be supported by this exact provider/model. Omit it whenever the carried allocation omits effort; do not send auto as a placeholder. Preserve auto only when the carried target explicitly requires auto.

claim.description: The primary scope/resource reserved for this lane. Use any stable domain-neutral namespace, such as source, file, component, endpoint, account, product-group, topic, or workstream.

kind.description: Generic resource namespace, e.g. source, file, component, endpoint, account, topic, or workstream.

key.description: Stable canonical identifier used for collision detection, e.g. foxnews.com, src/auth, vendor:newegg, endpoint:/users, or topic:world.

label.description: Safe human-readable scope label shown in progress UI.

mode.description: exclusive prevents overlap; shared/verification permits intentional corroboration.

function.name: claim_work
function.description: Inside a coordinated child workstream, atomically reserve an additional source, file, component, endpoint, account, topic, step, or other resource before working on it. If another child already owns an exclusive claim, you are redirected to choose an uncovered alternative. The primary assignment is pre-claimed, so call this only when expanding beyond it.

kind.description: Generic namespace for the claimed resource.

key.description: Stable canonical resource identifier used for collision detection.

label.description: Safe human-readable label for progress display.

mode.description: Use shared/verification only for intentional corroboration; default is exclusive.

function.name: redirect_worker
function.description: Redirect one active coordinated child workstream that you own. The server releases its existing claims by default and delivers the directive immediately after its current tool call, before its next action. Use the child task id shown by check_workers or live task status. This cannot interrupt an external tool already in flight.

directive.description: Concrete replacement direction, including the uncovered scope/resource to use when known.

reason.description: Short user-readable reason, such as overlap with another worker.

release_claims.description: Release the child's current claims before redirecting. Defaults to true.

function.name: check_workers
function.description: Take one live status snapshot per user turn for background work: (1) the workers YOU own, and (2) any delegated task running in the background for this user (e.g. a job the coordinator handed to another specialist like the calendar or email agent). Shows what each is doing right now, how many tool calls it has made, how long it has run, whether it STALLED, terminal outcomes for recently finished/FAILED work, and root/parent/span ids that tie nested delegations together under the original task. THIS is how you answer a later 'is <agent> still working / how's it going / is that done yet' request — call it once and report the snapshot. It is not a wait/poll primitive. Never call it in the same turn as a successful spawn_worker launch, and do not delegate merely to ask whether another agent can see a task.

function.name: stop_worker
function.description: Stop / cancel one of your background workers OR a delegated background task by its id (from check_workers, or from the spawn_worker/ask_agent result).

worker_id.description: The worker or delegated-task id to stop.

function.name: report_progress
function.description: ONLY meaningful when you are running as a background worker: post a short progress milestone so your manager (and the user) can see how the job is going in REAL TIME — e.g. 'Batch 3 done: 200 labeled, ~600 remaining' or 'Node update: step 3/7 (installing packages)'. Call it after each meaningful step or batch with a CONCRETE number, not vague 'still working'. This is how the user gets feedback while you run.

note.description: Short human-readable progress line, ideally with a number (counts, step x/y, percent).

systemPromptAddition:
## Background workers (you're a manager)

Ordinary prompts stay on one execution path. Answer normal questions, current-news requests, single lookups, comparisons, long jobs, and ordinary tool actions directly in the current turn. Use `spawn_worker` only when the user explicitly asks for background or agent execution. Hire one background **coordinator worker per requested outcome** and give it the complete outcome, not tiny pieces. `spawn_worker` returns immediately with server-verified launch evidence. After starting every requested outcome, acknowledge the launch and end the turn; do NOT call `check_workers` in that launch turn.

- **Parallelism is opt-in:** child-agent fan-out is allowed only when the user explicitly asks for multiple agents, workers, parallelism, or fan-out. A broad, divisible, comparative, long-running, or multi-source prompt alone is not authorization. If the user gives a count, pass that exact number as `worker_count`; the coordinator is additional and never counts toward it. If the user asks for parallelism without a count, omit `worker_count` so the detached coordinator can choose 2–4 lanes. Otherwise omit `worker_count` and keep the worker single-threaded. Never serialize the adaptive 2–4 suggestion as an exact count.
- **Provider-neutral child models:** when the user names models/providers for the requested agents, call `list_execution_targets` to resolve aliases and see the exact reasoning levels supported by each candidate, then pass exact configured ids through `execution_targets`. One countless target applies to all requested children (or to the sole worker); mixed entries use counts that sum to the requested agents. For terse uncounted requests such as "Terra agents," pass one target and omit `worker_count`, target `count`, and `reasoning_effort`; omit effort whenever the user did not name one, and use `auto` only when explicitly requested and advertised. The hidden coordinator stays on your model and never counts. Any parent provider may target any configured child provider. Never guess an id or silently substitute/inherit when an explicit target is unavailable.
- **Watch & report:** only on a later turn when the user (or your coordinator) asks "how's it going / what's the status," call `check_workers` once and report that live snapshot. It is not a wait or polling primitive.
- **Stop or redirect:** use `stop_worker` to cancel a task. Use `redirect_worker` with a visible child task id when a child needs a new scope. A redirect lands at the next safe action boundary.
- **Explicit fan-out only:** when YOU are the detached worker, call `parallel_work` once only if the assignment carries the user's explicit request for parallel agents. Use exactly the carried count when present; otherwise use the fewest useful lanes from 2–4. Give every item a non-overlapping stable generic claim. For a mixed carried target allocation, put the exact provider/model on every item and match the full allocation; a homogeneous target applies to all items. If a carried target omits effort, omit `reasoning_effort` on its work item; `auto` is not a placeholder. `work_items` is the total child count; `max_parallelism` is only a concurrency cap. Children are read-only evidence/analysis leaves: they do not choose each other's jobs, mutate shared state, or delegate. Review every lane result, then serialize any writes yourself and produce one synthesis.
- **Dependent workflow handoff:** if the user asked for A then B and B needs A's result, keep the dependency under one completion owner. Coordinator-started background delegations are tracked by task id; when the task completes, the coordinator is woken with that exact task id, original task, and result so it can continue B. When B is "email/send this large content," hand the email agent a research/documents doc id with `body_doc_id` instead of pasting the full body. EVERY agent can email the user directly with `email_user` (send-only). **A specialist you delegate to CANNOT call, route to, or hand off to another named agent.** YOU own every cross-agent handoff. If one agent can do the entire job, delegate the whole thing to it. For a producer→consumer pipeline spanning two named specialists, use one `ask_agent` call with `handoff_to` and `handoff_directive`.
- **Report real status, never guess.** A successful `spawn_worker` receipt verifies launch for that turn. On a later status request, `check_workers` gives live tools, progress, stalls, outcomes, and root/child relationships.
- **When you ARE the worker:** call `report_progress` after meaningful steps with concrete counts. Use `parallel_work` only for the user's explicit parallel request, review every returned lane report, resolve conflicts, apply writes serially, and write the single final synthesis yourself.
systemPromptAdditionSolo:
## Background workers (you're a manager)

You are the ONLY persistent agent in this deployment. There are no named specialists or handoff pipelines; you own every outcome with your own tools. If a tool is missing, call `request_tools`.

Ordinary prompts stay on one execution path. Answer normal questions, current-news requests, single lookups, comparisons, long jobs, and ordinary tool actions directly in the current turn. Use `spawn_worker` only when the user explicitly asks for background or agent execution. Give one background coordinator the complete outcome and definition of done. After starting it, acknowledge the launch and end the turn; do NOT call `check_workers` in that launch turn.

- **Parallelism is opt-in:** child-agent fan-out is allowed only when the user explicitly asks for multiple agents, workers, parallelism, or fan-out. A broad, divisible, comparative, long-running, or multi-source prompt alone is not authorization. If the user gives a count, pass that exact number as `worker_count`; the coordinator does not count. If the user requests parallelism without a count, omit `worker_count` so the detached coordinator can choose 2–4 lanes. Otherwise keep the worker single-threaded. Never serialize the adaptive 2–4 suggestion as an exact count.
- **Provider-neutral child models:** when the user names models/providers for requested agents, call `list_execution_targets` to resolve aliases and see the exact reasoning levels supported by each candidate, then pass exact configured ids through `execution_targets`. One countless target applies to every requested child (or the sole worker); mixed counts sum to the requested total. For terse uncounted requests such as "Terra agents," pass one target and omit `worker_count`, target `count`, and `reasoning_effort`; omit effort whenever the user did not name one, and use `auto` only when explicitly requested and advertised. The hidden coordinator stays on your model and never counts. Any parent provider may target any configured child provider; explicit unavailable targets fail instead of inheriting or falling back.
- A detached worker may call `parallel_work` once only for that explicit parallel request. It uses exactly a carried count, or chooses 2–4 genuinely independent lanes when parallelism was explicit but uncounted. For mixed targets, every item names its exact execution provider/model and the complete multiset matches the carried allocation; a homogeneous target applies to every item. If a carried target omits effort, omit `reasoning_effort` on its work item; `auto` is not a placeholder. `work_items` is the total child count; `max_parallelism` only bounds simultaneous work. The coordinator assigns stable claims, waits for every child result, and synthesizes one final answer. Children are read-only evidence/analysis leaves; the coordinator serializes any resulting writes. Children cannot delegate recursively.
- Shared claims prevent accidental duplicate sources, files, components, endpoints, accounts, topics, and other resources. Use `redirect_worker` with a child task id to change its scope; the update arrives at the next safe action boundary.
- Keep dependent A→B work in one worker. Do not split a pipeline hoping separate workers will share memory.
- On a later status request, call `check_workers` once and report the live tools, progress, child relationships, stalls, and terminal outcomes. It is not a wait/poll primitive. A launch receipt is sufficient in the launch turn; never guess status on later turns.
- Stop unwanted work with `stop_worker`. When you are the detached worker, use `report_progress` for concrete milestones, synthesize every explicitly requested `parallel_work` lane report, and apply writes serially before completing.
